slides.headline: October 6, 1949: Nehru laid the foundation stone for a military academy unlike any other in the world.
Jawaharlal Nehru laid the foundation stone of the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla
slides.body: The academy was designed as the world's first tri-service military academy - training Army, Navy and Air Force cadets together from day one, instead of separately. The original paperwork called it the 'National War Academy'; Nehru objected to the name at the ceremony itself and had it changed to 'National Defence Academy.'

slides.headline: It would take over five years before the first cadets walked through its gates.
slides.body: The NDA was formally commissioned on December 7, 1954, and inaugurated on January 16, 1955 - becoming the training ground for generations of India's military leadership, built around a tri-service model many countries still don't use.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needed its defense institutions built for integration, not separation, from the start.
slides.body: Nehru's small edit to the academy's name - from 'war' to 'defence' - still frames how India's military has trained its officers for over 75 years.

sources.text: The Week - Khadakwasla: The cradle of India's military leadership
